newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Two blasts rock Tajik capital, one person killed.
newsitem.headline: Two blasts rock Tajik capital, one person killed.

text.p: Two explosions rocked the centre of the Tajik capital Dushanbe on Thursday, killing one person and injuring another, witnesses said.
Reuter correspondent Yuri Kushko saw a corpse lying near Dushanbe's main post office and bystanders said an injured person had been taken to hospital after an explosion near the building.
Kushko also saw a wrecked Lada car near the Pakistan embassy, scene of the second blast.
It was not immediately clear what caused the explosions, which both occurred after midday (0700 GMT). The buildings were quickly sealed off by police who refused to comment.
The explosions smashed windows in nearby buildings only hours after a ceasefire had been due to come into effect in the former Soviet republic, which is wracked by civil war.
Nerves in the Tajik capital are on edge following a spate of attacks against Russian servicemen who help prop up Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov's shaky administration.
The recent attacks have been widely blamed on opposition guerrillas, but the opposition has not claimed responsibility.

Rakhmonov and Islamic opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri agreed the ceasefire -- which was supposed to come into effect at midnight local time on Wednesday -- during talks in northern Afghanistan earlier this week in preparation for signing a peace agreement in Moscow on December 19.

But many previous accords have been routinely flouted in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China, despite efforts to end a four-year civil war which has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced many more.
